title: Ben-Gvir Leads Over 2,000 Israelis Into Al-Aqsa Compound on Tisha B'Av
detail: Israeli far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir led a mass entry of Israeli Jews into Jerusalem's Al-Aqsa Mosque compound to mark Tisha B'Av, the Jewish fasting day commemorating the destruction of the First and Second Temples. Reports put the number of participants between roughly 2,250 and over 3,200, entering in groups under Israeli police protection and singing Jewish hymns — a breach of the site's decades-old status quo reserving worship there for Muslims. Jordan condemned the incursion. The episode became a flashpoint that, alongside further incursions in the following weeks, prompted Jordan to convene an emergency meeting of Arab and Islamic foreign ministers on August 5 over what it called an 'imminent' Israeli move to alter control of the site.

media.caption: Itamar Ben-Gvir enters the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound with Israeli worshippers on Tisha B'Av — July 23, 2026
